panels.title: Inbound vs Outbound Peers
panels.description: Number of inbound and outbound TCP peer connections. Validators typically show 0 inbound.

panels.title: Peer Latency
panels.description: Round-trip latency to connected peers in milliseconds. Avg/min/max give a distribution across all current connections. Y-axis capped at 500ms — outlier peers near disconnect threshold may exceed this.

panels.title: Consensus Disputes
panels.description: Transactions in dispute during the current consensus round — those not agreed upon by all UNL validators. Resets each round (~3s). Spikes are normal during high throughput.

panels.title: Network Fees (drops)
panels.description: Transaction fees in drops of XRP (1 XRP = 1,000,000 drops). Open Ledger fee rises when demand is high. Base fee is the minimum; median reflects actual market rate.

panels.title: Transaction Queue
panels.description: Transactions waiting in the queue (Queue), currently being applied to the open ledger (Current Ledger), and the expected count based on recent history (Expected).

panels.title: Version Spread
panels.description: Current peer count per rippled version. A mix is normal during rolling upgrades.

panels.title: Cache Hit Rates
panels.description: Percentage of ledger and node-read cache lookups served from cache. Higher is better. A sustained drop can indicate memory pressure or a cold restart.

panels.title: DB Queue & Write Load
panels.description: Pending database read requests (Read Queue) and current write load. Sustained elevation indicates I/O bottleneck on the node's storage backend.

panels.title: IO Latency
panels.description: Time rippled waits on I/O operations in milliseconds. Values consistently above 1ms suggest storage or system I/O bottleneck.

panels.title: Load Factor
panels.description: Load factor components. Network = fee-scaling load broadcast to peers. Server = this node's own local load. Fee Escalation > 1 means transaction fees are being artificially inflated. Fee Queue > 1 means the transaction queue is adding pressure on fees.

panels.title: Load Threads
panels.description: Number of threads active in rippled's job scheduler. Increasing thread count under load is normal. Continuously maxed-out threads may indicate processing backlog.

panels.title: Transaction Queue Overflow
panels.description: Transactions rejected because the queue was full since rippled startup. Any non-zero value means clients are being turned away — indicates sustained congestion.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since rippled last started. A reset indicates a restart.

panels.title: Peer Disconnects / min
panels.description: Rate of peer disconnects per minute derived from rippled's cumulative counter. Baseline churn of ~1–2/min is normal. Sustained spikes may indicate network instability or resource pressure.

panels.title: Endpoint Scrape Success
panels.description: Per-endpoint scrape health. OK = exporter successfully called that rippled RPC method last cycle. FAIL = the call errored or timed out.

panels.title: Scrape Duration
panels.description: Time taken to complete one full scrape cycle across all rippled RPC endpoints. Spikes here do not affect Prometheus scrape timeouts but indicate rippled is slow to respond.

panels.title: Ledger History Range
panels.description: Number of complete ledgers stored locally. Climbs steadily as new ledgers close, then drops sharply at each NuDB rotation cycle.

panels.title: Ledger Fetch Activity
panels.description: Active: ledgers currently in the fetch queue. Incomplete: not yet fully acquired. Timeouts: cumulative fetch timeouts across all active acquisitions. Sustained incomplete > 0 or rising timeouts may indicate sync issues or network stress.

panels.title: Ledger Age
panels.description: Age of the last validated ledger in seconds. Should stay under 5s during normal operation. Spikes indicate consensus delays or network issues.

panels.title: Reserve: Base
panels.description: Base account reserve in XRP. Changes require an amendment.

panels.title: Reserve: Owner Increment
panels.description: Reserve increment in XRP per object owned by an account (offers, trust lines, etc.).

panels.title: State Accounting
panels.description: Cumulative seconds spent in each server state since startup. Use this to assess node stability — a healthy node spends nearly all time in 'full' or 'proposing'.

panels.title: State Transitions
panels.description: Rate of transitions into each server state per minute. Spikes in non-full states indicate instability.

panels.title: Validator List Site Health
panels.description: Current fetch status per validator list site. Green = UP (last fetch accepted), red = DOWN (last fetch failed). A failed fetch doesn't immediately affect validation but will cause issues when the current list expires.

panels.title: Non-sane Peers
panels.description: Number of connected peers with non-sane status (insane or unknown). Should always be 0. Non-zero values indicate peers behaving unexpectedly.

panels.title: Database Sizes
panels.description: NuDB/RocksDB on-disk size in KB for the ledger store and transaction store. Monitor for growth to plan storage capacity.

panels.title: DB Read / Write Ops
panels.description: Rate of read and write operations to the NuDB/RocksDB object store. High write rates under sustained load are normal. Unexpected spikes may indicate replay or resync activity.

panels.title: UNL Size
panels.description: Number of trusted validators in the UNL (Unique Node List). Compare against validation_quorum to understand headroom.

panels.title: Validations Cached
panels.description: Number of validator signatures currently held in the validation cache.

panels.title: Validation Quorum
panels.description: Minimum number of trusted validators required to reach consensus. Compare against UNL Size to understand headroom.

panels.title: Amendments Enabled
panels.description: Total number of amendments currently active on this network.

panels.title: Amendments Pending
panels.description: Amendments that have reached the voting threshold and are in the 2-week activation window. Non-zero means a network upgrade is imminent — ensure rippled is up to date.

panels.title: Amendments Near Threshold
panels.description: Amendments with >= 75% of required votes but not yet at the activation threshold. Monitor these to anticipate upcoming network changes.

panels.title: Last Scrape Success Age
panels.description: Seconds since the last fully successful scrape. Spikes indicate the exporter is failing to reach rippled.
